$schema-note: Reproducibility manifest for one unit's art. Copy this file to art/units/<unit>/manifest.json and fill it in. Its purpose: any frame can be regenerated identically later, and the dataset is self-documenting for AI training. See docs/art-generation.md.

generation.styleFragment: soft hand-painted 2D game sprite, high-angle 3/4 top-down view, chibi proportions with large rounded head and small stout body and short stubby limbs, soft volumetric cel shading, single soft light from top-left, gentle gradient form shadows, soft ambient occlusion, crisp rim highlight, thin dark desaturated outline, cohesive muted palette of teal slate-blue warm-sand and soft-green, bold readable silhouette, cute by proportion not by expression, single character centered, transparent background, no cast ground shadow, consistent line weight, game asset, clean edges
generation.unitPrompt: FILL_IN — the unit-specific line from art/style/prompts-units.md
generation.negativePrompt: side view, front orthographic view, flat orthographic, isometric grid, realistic human proportions, tall lanky body, heavy black comic ink outline, cel-shaded anime, harsh cast shadow on ground, busy background, scenery, multiple characters, text, watermark, signature, logo, oversaturated neon colors, gradient background, photorealistic, 3d render, blurry, low contrast, extra limbs, deformed hands, exaggerated screaming face, bulging eyes

handEditing: FILL_IN — describe any manual cleanup/compositing done. (Relevant both for reproducibility and because meaningful human editing is what can make the assembled sprite sheet copyrightable, if that is ever wanted.)
deployedTo: UnityRTS/RTS/Assets/... (path where the finished sheet is imported into Unity)
